subject.title: Plugins cannot intercept inbound messages on the embedded agent path: global inbound_claim wrapper exists but is never invoked, and before_agent_reply is gated to trigger === "cron"

question: Should ordinary channel traffic remain on the documented `before_agent_run` blocking contract, or should plugins gain a new global interception point before session/agent routing?
rationale: Current tests deliberately keep global `inbound_claim` off ordinary traffic, while current docs provide a later transcript-safe blocker; changing the earlier boundary affects plugin ordering, routing ownership, failure policy, and potentially multiple plugins claiming the same message.

options.title: Clarify and use before_agent_run
options.body: Keep `inbound_claim` binding-owned, document that scope, and provide a tested `before_agent_run` pattern for suppressing self-echoes before model input.

options.title: Broadcast inbound_claim globally
options.body: Invoke the existing global runner for ordinary traffic and define priority, timeout, failure, reply-delivery, and multi-plugin claim semantics as a public plugin contract.

options.title: Add a distinct pre-routing hook
options.body: Preserve `inbound_claim` ownership semantics while adding a narrowly named hook for global suppression or routing before canonical session selection.

recommendation.title: Clarify and use before_agent_run
recommendation.body: Keep `inbound_claim` binding-owned, document that scope, and provide a tested `before_agent_run` pattern for suppressing self-echoes before model input.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history ties this person to the conversation-binding and inbound-claim dispatch boundary that the decision would change.
